title: Grid
description: Turn the background grid on, set its spacing and subdivisions, and snap drawing to it.

bubble.title: The Grid section
bubble.body: The grid is a background ruler laid over the page: evenly spaced points or lines to measure and snap against. It is document state — it saves with the file.

bubble.title: Turn the grid on
bubble.body: Switch on Grid in the Grid section (the / key does it too). The page gains its dotted measuring grid.

bubble.title: Set the spacing
bubble.body: Set Spacing to 40. The grid breathes out — every cell is now 40 points wide.

bubble.title: Snap to it
bubble.body: In the Snapping section, switch on Grid snapping. Points you place now land on grid intersections instead of between them.

bubble.title: Finer detail
bubble.body: Subdivisions splits each cell into smaller steps for snapping without crowding the page, and Style switches the dots to full lines. A diamond grid is under Type.
